title: Governed Self-Improvement for a Local-First Security Analyzer: Baseline Measurements and a Preregistered Evaluation Protocol for Tantular Cyber
read_level: full (v1 PDF, 2-column text extracted; all sections read)
why_wsp: Proposes weight-space edits as rung 4 of an intervention ladder for improving a local security-explanation model, but no weight edit is performed; the paper reports only scanner/explanation baselines and a preregistered protocol.
domain: local-first static code security analysis; Bahasa Indonesia vulnerability explanations
editor: none run; proposed 'proposer (scripts or an AI controller)'
target: tantular-cyber local model (Q8_0, Ollama); compared with qwen3:8b. Parameter count of Tantular model not stated beyond 'a different 8B model' comparison; weight-edit rung would first replicate the published edit on its original 0.8B model
interface: other (proposed ladder: prompt, context, LoRA/QLoRA, weight-space edit)
self_editing: no; 'self-improving' means an automated loop up to a human gate, and the loop has not been run

headline_results.quote: combining Semgrep with an interprocedural call-graph scanner yields precision 0.843 and recall 0.915 (Semgrep alone: 0.818 and 0.766)
only 57% of Tantular's explanations were grounded in the evidence shown, against 95% for a different 8B model

headline_results.claim: Concise prompt raised grounding partly by citing nothing
headline_results.quote: The concise profile cited nothing in 8 of 80 samples (baseline: 0 of 80); counting abstention as ungrounded lowers its rate from 0.72 to 0.65.
An audit of our own artifacts found that the published 57% cannot be reproduced
The loop has not been run; no fine-tuned or weight-edited Tantular model exists

cost.where: Table II (p50 s column: 25.9 s; qwen3:8b 12.9 s)

baselines_and_controls: Scanner ablation (Semgrep only, callgraph only); paired comparison with qwen3:8b; prompt and context-window interventions under a preregistered adoption rule. No weight-editing baselines (none run).
runs_and_variance: "40 FINDINGS x 3 SEEDS (n = 120 PER MODEL)" with Wilson 95% intervals and exact McNemar tests (Table II, Sec IV-A).
robustness_of_edits: not tested (no edits made); protocol states rungs 3-4 produce a new checkpoint 'which is quantized and evaluated again as its own artifact'
verification: Preregistered protocol with hard gates (Table V), paired Clopper-Pearson bounds, bootstrap, Benjamini-Hochberg; not yet executed. No formal verification.
limitations_stated: Loop not run; no weight-edited model exists; all rates from 33 synthetic Python cases, one machine, one Ollama version; grounding check is a lexical proxy; model comparison confounded with quantization; own published 57% not reproducible.
cites_or_builds_on: Weight-space programming [13] (Takehi et al. blog, per text: 'edits a small fraction of a model's weights directly ... 0.8B model on a mathematics benchmark')
notes_for_survey: Positions weight-space editing as the most expensive rung of a governed improvement ladder that must beat prompt and LoRA changes on identical items, with a planned replication of the original 0.8B edit before use. Contains no WSP experiments; relevant only as a governance/protocol proposal and for its documented evaluation hazards (silent model-file migration).
